how: A member proposes drawing together and another supplies a draft that attracts further design requests.
Repeated calls gather hands around a shared image, pool scattered efforts, and request backup during placement.
Builders judge the larger image beyond their numbers and available calm space.
Members draft a gate, request lettering and animation, then reduce the image to fit available effort.
Members report pixels placed, a ministargate underway, and completion of the tiny gate.
Members request coordinates and specify a black border and yellow-dotted area that constrain placement.
Acceptance that depends on missing coordinates or backup must remain distinct from a bare commitment asking nothing back.
A script is discussed as a possible alternative to shrinking, while actual execution remains unobserved.
Guest sanction is explicit, but this room cannot test the aggregate prevalence claim or establish its own internal decision procedure.
The completed gate receives protective boundaries and is favored for low maintenance while larger projects remain optional.
Participants attribute the loss of a forming ring to a neighboring lattice refill.
Members propose asking for reserved space and later report official sanction for a tiny site.
A small guest image occupies sanctioned host territory and its defenders are instructed to preserve the surrounding lattice.
The completed gate's instructions explicitly preserve surrounding lattice and neighboring designs.
Participants request help from another group and credit outside helpers without documenting a reciprocal bargain.
One participant reports asking another group for help or space on the builders' behalf.
Outside help and an outsider's Discord invitation do not establish coalition membership by the builders.
After erasure and defended locations, participants abandon spots and seek smaller builds elsewhere.
Reported sanction and host procedures contain no coded dispute over who can bind the guest room to an agreement.
The coded erasure instruction names flags without identifying an inherited quarrel.
Existing fandom symbols and lore supply the proposed gate, lettering, point of origin, and animation.
No preexisting tie is named as the reason for the coded call to erase flags.
A fake actor-death announcement invokes April Fools and provokes objections to its timing and official-looking presentation.
The moderator apology regulates the room's own fake-death joke and does not evidence restrictions on canvas talk.
Participants celebrate survival and claim collective accomplishment, while the final title leaves the claimed object unspecified.
Participants recount defeated attempts and report that the small gate remained when placement ended.
Considering successor venues must retain the distinction between conditional interest and a demonstrated choice or move.
Survival reports and a title-only accomplishment claim do not show disputes about cleanup or which historical version to preserve.
One participant calls for erasing flags in reply to an outside recruiter without demonstrating collective adoption or execution.
Reports of defeat and one erasure instruction do not establish a sustained exchange of taunts or victory claims with a rival.
A drawing call is followed in its thread by placement reports and efforts to pool resources.
The opening proposal already includes recruitment, so a separate starter-to-call mechanism cannot be distinguished.
The completion announcement identifies the placed gate as the object of immediate protective instructions.
Negotiating access can precede completion and successful upkeep rather than arising only after a secure mark stands.
The host location explicitly grounds instructions to spare its surrounding lattice and neighboring designs.
Pressure can lead to shrinking into low-maintenance sanctioned space while automation remains only a proposal.
Completion is announced together with credit to helpers, followed by explicit celebration of survival.
One survival report both celebrates and records the outcome, leaving a distinct causal passage between those acts unestablished.
Recording survival can be followed by deferring a successor choice rather than committing to continuation.
A builder explicitly explains moving to a much smaller version through insufficient numbers and calm space.
A draft and later boundary instructions are visible, but neither proves that posting a template settled design disagreement.
A participant joins while requesting coordinates, so acceptance can make further information due.
Help requests precede final upkeep instructions, and the record does not trace strain through a request to a named helper's response.
Sanctioned space and credited Samurai help coexist without evidence that border talks produced that help.
The visible attack call answers outside recruitment, so its production by the builders' earlier recruitment remains unestablished.
The later neighbor-preserving instructions do not answer or recall the isolated flag-erasure call.
No coded passage makes the isolated erasure call the reason for subsequent negotiations.
No coded response develops the flag-erasure call into a continuing verbal contest.
Credited outside helpers and an invitation to another group's Discord do not demonstrate a defense coalition formed under upkeep strain.
Canvas recruitment is visible without coded evidence that it triggered moderation of canvas discussion.
Host sanction is reported without a coded follow-up disputing who may commit the guest room.
Successful completion in contested space can depend on obtaining host approval before rebuilding.
Securing a sanctioned tiny site supplies the location subsequently identified in the completion account.
Repeated losses are followed by a smaller sanctioned completion, reopening construction after relocation.
Members contest the joke's timing, official confirmation, and suitability, while proposing more obviously fictional alternatives.
Moderators acknowledge harm, remove official-looking endorsement, and offer text flairs as repair for their separate prank.
Neighbor-preserving completion rules cannot be generalized to every participant when another explicitly endorses erasure.
A collective title claim with a deleted body cannot identify its drawing or establish continuity with an earlier completed gate.
A member defers choosing a successor canvas until others converge on one, leaving continuation unresolved.
